question.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy+yz+xz)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy+yz+xz)\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(xy+yz+xz)\,k \\  & =(y+z)\,i+(x+z)\,j+(y+x)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=t,y={e}^{t},$ and $z=e$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =({e}^{t}+e)\,i+(t+e)\,j+({e}^{t}+t)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(e)\,k \\  & =i+{e}^{t}\,j+(0)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(({e}^{t}+e)\,i+(t+e)\,j+({e}^{t}+t)\,k)\cdot (i+{e}^{t}\,j+(0)\,k) \\  & =({e}^{t}+e)\cdot 1+(t+e)\cdot {e}^{t}+({e}^{t}+t)\cdot 0 \\  & ={e}^{t}+e+t{e}^{t}+{e}^{t+1} \\  & ={e}^{t+1}+(1+t){e}^{t}+e.\end{aligned}
$$
